requirements.text: clamp(x, lo, hi) returns lo when x < lo, hi when x > hi, and x otherwise (for lo <= hi).
requirements.reason: The claim says the function always returns x, even when x is outside the bounds. For example, it returns 1 for clamp(1, 2, 3), while the requirement says it should return 2.

claims.summary: The exported clamp function always returns its first 32-bit input unchanged, regardless of the other two inputs.
claims.statement:
∀ (x lo hi : BitVec 32),
  FVA.Wasm.Exec.Returns Examples.Mislabeled.Lifted.module "clamp"
    [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 lo, FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 hi] [FVA.Wasm.Exec.Val.i32 x]
claims.name: Examples.Mislabeled.clamp
claims.intent: `clamp(x, lo, hi)` on signed 32-bit ints: `x` clamped into the range `[lo, hi]`.
details: Covers every combination of three 32-bit WebAssembly integer inputs: x, lo, and hi. They are treated as raw 32-bit values; the claim does not interpret any input as signed or unsigned for comparison, and no arithmetic or wraparound is specified.
For every host behavior, the module can be instantiated, and calling the exported function named clamp terminates without trapping and returns exactly the first input, x.
